equivalents.note: The Tibetan heading renders rāga as glu dbyangs 'melody', transliterates the name as de sha kha, and adds the poet, nag po spyod pa'i zhabs, whom the Bengali heading does not name.
Throughout the song the Tibetan translates Ḍombī with the common noun g.yung mo 'low-caste woman' instead of transliterating the name.
khyim is 'house, home' rather than a word for a hut, matching Munidatta's tavāgāra 'your house', which cp.10.m2 renders khyod kyi khyim.

The Tibetan has bram ze'i bu 'brahmin's son, brahmin boy' for bāhma nāṛiā, apparently taking nāṛiā as 'lad' rather than 'shaven-headed', in line with Munidatta's cittavaṭuka, which cp.10.m2 renders sems ni bram ze'i bu.
The verse transliterates the vernacular name (Kāhna), while the heading and the commentary use the Tibetan name nag po spyod pa (see cp.10.m1).
Here kāpāli is rendered adjectivally, thod pa'i rnal 'byor 'skull yogi', whereas 6a transliterates it (ka pA li) and cp.10.m7 has thod pa can.
Rendered analytically as skyug bro spangs, 'having given up revulsion'.

The Tibetan compresses 'one lotus, sixty-four petals' into gcig nyid pad 'dab 'the one, lotus petals', so the lotus appears only as the first member of the compound pad 'dab (the commentary has the full pad+ma).

In this line caṛi 'climbing' becomes der gnas 'staying there' (matching Munidatta's tatra sthitvā), and bāpuṛī seems to be transliterated (pa pu lI'i or pu lI'i after gar byed) rather than translated.
rgyud, a word that also means 'tantra' and 'lineage', renders both tānti here and Munidatta's tantrī in cp.10.m6.
Transliterated here (ka pA li), unlike the translated thod pa'i of 2b.
rdzing bu is 'pond, pool'; cp.10.m8 uses the same word for sarovara and renders kāyapuṣkara as lus kyi rdzing bu 'the pool of the body'.

The Tibetan makes Ḍombī the object of 'taking' (g.yung mo blangs nas 'having taken the g.yung mo') and ends bdag gi pha rol gsod 'I kill the other (or: my adversary)', apparently reading parāṇa as para 'other' rather than prāṇa 'life'.
Munidatta's nairātmadharma is bdag med pa'i chos 'the dharma of selflessness', with the abstract bdag med pa rather than the goddess's name bdag med ma.
The commentary uses the Tibetan name nag po spyod pa'i zhabs for Kṛṣṇapāda (also nag po zhabs in cp.10.m2 and nag po spyod pa pa in cp.10.m4), against the transliterated kAh+Na of verse 2b.
The Tibetan renders the term as dgongs pa'i skad 'language of intention', reading sandhā/saṃdhā 'intention' rather than sandhyā 'twilight', and renders ḍombīśabda as g.yung mo'i sgra.
Transliterated (a wa d+hU tI) rather than translated with kun 'dar ma, here and in cp.10.m8 (a wa d+hU tI pa yongs su ma dag pa can).

bdag med mar renders the identification of Ḍombī with Nairātmā; later in the segment the vocative bho nairātmā is joined to the next lemma as kye bdag med ma'i grong khyer la, 'O, to Nairātmā's town'.
Munidatta's cittavaṭuka 'mind-lad' becomes a sentence, sems ni bram ze'i bu 'the mind is the brahmin boy', reusing the verse's bram ze'i bu.

sampradāya is rendered man ngag 'instruction', and the Tibetan reads asampradāyayogināṃ positively as man ngag thob pa'i rnal 'byor pa 'the yogin who has obtained the instruction', without the negation.
siddhācārya is grub pa'i slob dpon here, not the grub thob recorded in the glossary.
The Tibetan turns nirghṛṇa into one of the faults listed, skyug bro ba dang ngo tsha ba la sogs pa'i skyon dang bral ba 'free of faults such as revulsion and shame', instead of a separate predicate.
The Tibetan reverses the pair to thabs dang shes rab 'means and wisdom', here and in the Hevajra quotation, unlike the glossary's shes rab dang thabs.
The Tibetan names the tantra dpal dgyes pa'i rdo rje 'glorious Hevajra' (so also in cp.10.m4 and cp.10.m5), not the kye'i rdo rje'i rgyud recorded in the glossary.

The Tibetan places the lotus in the wheel (sprul pa'i 'khor lor pad+ma 'dab ma drug cu rtsa bzhi dang ldan pa 'in the wheel of emanation, a lotus with sixty-four petals') rather than equating the two as padmaikaṃ nirmāṇacakraṃ does.
The Tibetan counts as Munidatta does, rkang pa gsum pa 'third verse' for couplet 4 (and rkang pa gnyis pa for couplet 3 in cp.10.m4), leaving the refrain out.

The Tibetan fuses sadbhāvena svarūpāśayena into bden pa'i dngos po'i rang bzhin gyi bsam pas 'with the thought of the nature of the true thing', while the Hevajra quotation in the same segment renders svarūpa as ngo bo and ngo bo nyid.
Here nairātmadharmasvarūpa is chos thams cad bdag med pa'i ngo bo nyid, so svarūpa is ngo bo nyid, as in the Hevajra quotation of cp.10.m5, while the glosses in cp.10.m5 and cp.10.m7 use rang bzhin.
Transliterated (b+ha ga) and followed by pad+ma'i gnas su 'as the place of the lotus'.
yul gyi snang ba 'appearance of objects' supports reading viṣayābhāsa for the printed ṣiṣayābhāsaṃ; in cp.10.m2 the Tibetan has no word for viṣaya.
saṃsārapeṭaka 'the basket (or box) of saṃsāra' is rendered 'khor ba'i mdzod 'the treasury of saṃsāra'.
saprapañcacaryā is rendered spyod pa rab tu gsal bar gsungs 'explains the conduct very clearly', so saprapañca is read as describing the explanation rather than the conduct.

Here kāpālikaḥ caryādharaś ca becomes thod pa can gyi spyod pa 'dzin pa 'holding the conduct of a skull-bearer', and the Tibetan keeps Munidatta's letter-etymology in transliteration (kaM 'your bliss', pA 'able to protect').
The Tibetan reads the compound as 'the wheel of the six tathāgatas' (de bzhin gshegs pa drug gi 'khor lo), followed by earrings, necklace and bone ornaments (rus rgyan).
For gurusampradāyavihīnasya the Tibetan has bla ma'i drin gyis rnam par dman pa, with drin 'kindness, grace' where cp.10.m2 has man ngag, and its syntax ('deficient by the guru's grace') is loose.

questions: dombi, cp.10.4b: the Tibetan line ('ong dang 'gro ba gang gi gru la byed) has no word for Ḍombī, so no equivalent is given for this line.
dombi, cp.10.m6: bho ḍombi nairātme is rendered kye'i bdag med ma alone, with no g.yung mo.
visaya, cp.10.m2: rūpādiviṣayasamūhaṃ is rendered phyi rol gyi gzugs la sogs pa'i tshogs, with no word for viṣaya (phyi rol may stand for tasya bāhye); the equivalent is taken from cp.10.m6 instead.

Substring matches with no equivalent: siddha in cp.10.m3 (the word is siddhiṃ, given under siddhi); vajra in cp.10.m3, m4 and m5 (only inside śrīhevajre, given under tx-hevajra); citta in cp.10.m5 and m8 (only inside bodhicitta).

bhaga, cp.10.m4: a false match on bhagavatyā, which the Tibetan renders bcom ldan 'das; that belongs to p-bhagavat, but here it is an epithet of Nairātmā. Should p-bhagavat cover the feminine bhagavatī?

nairatma / nairatmya: in cp.10.m1 nairātmadharma is the abstract (bdag med pa'i chos) and is given under nairatmya; in cp.10.m2-m7 the Sanskrit has the goddess's name nairātmā (bdag med ma), given under nairatma at cp.10.m2 only, so the nairatmya matches in those segments are not answered.

Not repeated: commentary occurrences of terms that use the same Tibetan word as the verse or an earlier segment (dombi g.yung mo, town grong khyer, brahmin bram ze, boat gru, lotus pad+ma, tanti rgyud, lake rdzing bu, bodhicitta, samvrti, nairatma bdag med ma, tx-hevajra, avadhuti in cp.10.m8, p-kanha nag po spyod pa) are left out.
